session.agent-connection-instruction.meaning: An instruction handed from an open Human2AI session to an external Agent, containing the CLI command that discovers the current session, its latest capture, its UI URL, and its supported operations before the Agent waits for the user's next request.
session.agent-connection-instruction.scope: The shared session-details panel used by composition, UI-sketch, and 3D space workbenches.
session.agent-connection-instruction.referent: The current persisted Human2AI session and the machine-readable CLI connection command injected by the page.
session.agent-connection-instruction.precedence: It is the entry point for Agent collaboration; it precedes capture retrieval and type-specific processing, and differs from copying a prompt, preview image, or raw session identifier.
examples: Give an external Agent a session connect command from the composition workbench and ask it to wait after connecting.
nonExamples: Copy the image-generation prompt.
Copy a preview image from the current canvas.
List capture revisions without discovering the rest of the session contract.

session.agent-command-copy-action.meaning: Copy the current session Agent connection instruction, with instruction-specific pending and failure feedback. Success uses the shared clipboard.copied status.
session.agent-command-copy-action.scope: The shared session-details panel used by composition, UI-sketch, and 3D space workbenches.
session.agent-command-copy-action.referent: The complete localized Agent connection instruction generated for the current persisted session.
session.agent-command-copy-action.precedence: It acts on the session Agent connection instruction and differs from copying an image-generation prompt, a preview image, or a raw session identifier.
examples: Copy the generated human2ai session connect instruction from the session-details panel.
nonExamples: Copy an image-generation prompt from the canvas tools.
Copy or download the current preview image.
Copy a session identifier without the Agent connection instructions.

actions.delete.meaning: A destructive command that removes the target identified by the surrounding interface, after confirmation when confirmation is required.
actions.delete.scope: Shared product deletion controls: menu and button commands plus target-specific confirmation questions.
actions.delete.referent: The project, session, or other item made explicit by the current control or dialog.
actions.delete.precedence: None; this is an action rather than hierarchical content.
examples: A Delete item in an actions menu.
The destructive Delete button in a confirmation dialog.
nonExamples: Archiving an item without deleting it.
A sentence explaining what data deletion removes.
A Keep or Cancel action that dismisses deletion.

actions.keep.meaning: Dismiss a deletion confirmation and retain the targeted item.
actions.keep.scope: Deletion confirmations in composition and UI-sketch node editors.
actions.keep.referent: The node, region, or text element whose deletion is pending.
actions.keep.precedence: The non-destructive alternative to deletion; retaining the item does not undo its previously saved edits.
examples: Keep a region after opening its deletion confirmation.
nonExamples: Cancel a rename dialog.
Restore an already deleted item.

actions.cancel.meaning: Dismiss the current dialog or editor without executing its pending action. Already saved changes in an immediate-save editor remain saved; closing does not promise an undo.
actions.cancel.scope: Shared confirmation and editing controls across the product.
actions.cancel.referent: The currently open transient flow, rather than the underlying project, session, draft, or canvas content.
actions.cancel.precedence: Paired with the primary or destructive action presented by the same transient flow.
examples: Dismiss a clear-canvas confirmation without changing the canvas.
Close an immediate-save node editor without reverting saved changes.
nonExamples: Navigate back to a previous page.
Keep an item in a deletion confirmation when the product intentionally uses reassuring copy.

notes.global.meaning: The highest-level note that gives direction for the entire editable artifact and governs subordinate element notes when both are present.
notes.global.scope: Shared by composition drafts and UI sketches.
notes.global.referent: The whole composition draft or UI sketch being edited.
notes.global.precedence: Top-level; applies across node, region, text, and annotation notes rather than describing one element.
examples: Keep the entire interface quiet and emphasize the primary action.
Emphasize the subject on the left across the whole composition.
nonExamples: A note attached only to one region, text element, node, or annotation.
An internal implementation comment that users never see.

clipboard.group.meaning: Heading grouping tools that copy representations of the current artifact.
clipboard.group.precedence: A heading rather than an unspecified copy action.
examples: Heading above Copy prompt and Copy preview.
nonExamples: Copy selected text.

clipboard.prompt.meaning: Copy generated text instructions for the current artifact or selected UI stages.
clipboard.prompt.referent: The generated prompt determined by the active editor.
clipboard.prompt.precedence: Distinct from copying a rendered image or connection command.
examples: Copy layout instructions for a selected UI stage.
nonExamples: Copy a PNG preview.

clipboard.preview.meaning: Copy a PNG preview rendered from the authored artifact; download it if image clipboard access is unavailable.
clipboard.preview.scope: Composition and selected UI-sketch stage copy tools.
clipboard.preview.referent: The current authored composition or selected UI stage preview.
clipboard.preview.precedence: Same user-facing operation across renderers; excludes uploaded images and Agent-refined references.
examples: Copy the authored composition preview.
Copy the selected UI stage preview.
nonExamples: Switch to the Preview tab.
Copy an uploaded image node.

clipboard.success.meaning: The requested clipboard write completed successfully; the initiating control identifies its payload.
clipboard.success.precedence: A result independent of payload; excludes download, pending and failed operations.
examples: Show success after writing a prompt or command to the clipboard.
nonExamples: Report a download as a successful clipboard write.

canvas.visual-weight.meaning: The intended relative visual prominence of an element, independent of physical size and depth.
canvas.visual-weight.scope: Composition and UI-sketch element editors and exported prompts.
canvas.visual-weight.referent: An element relative to other elements in the artifact.
canvas.visual-weight.precedence: High, medium, low and decorative describe prominence; auto leaves it unspecified.
examples: Give the main subject high visual weight.
nonExamples: Foreground or background depth.
Physical height.

dimensions.width.meaning: The horizontal extent of a frame or its horizontal ratio component; units and interpretation come from the enclosing size or ratio control.
dimensions.width.scope: Composition ratio and UI interface size controls.
dimensions.width.referent: The horizontal input of the current frame control.
dimensions.width.precedence: Paired with the other dimension; unrelated to visual prominence.
examples: The width input in a width-to-height control.
nonExamples: High visual weight.

dimensions.height.meaning: The vertical extent of a frame or its vertical ratio component; units and interpretation come from the enclosing size or ratio control.
dimensions.height.scope: Composition ratio and UI interface size controls.
dimensions.height.referent: The vertical input of the current frame control.
dimensions.height.precedence: Paired with the other dimension; unrelated to visual prominence.
examples: The height input in a width-to-height control.
nonExamples: High visual weight.

notes.element.meaning: User instructions about the meaning or requirements of one canvas element.
notes.element.scope: Composition nodes and UI regions, text or images, including exported prompts.
notes.element.referent: The currently edited or numbered element.
notes.element.precedence: Subordinate to the global note; distinct from visible text and Agent-authored node descriptions. Reference-composition imports leave this field empty for the user, while preserving existing user notes.
examples: Ask the Agent to enlarge a region or change what it represents.
nonExamples: Requirements for the entire artifact.
Literal text to render.
An Agent's description of a visual group recovered from a reference picture.

text.content.meaning: The literal visible text content of a text element.
text.content.scope: Composition text regions and UI-sketch text elements.
text.content.referent: Text that appears in the output.
text.content.precedence: Distinct from instructions about the text; blank input retains domain-specific behavior in its placeholder.
examples: The exact title printed in a text region.
nonExamples: A note describing the title mood.

service.sync-error.meaning: The editor could not synchronize with Human2AI and displays the supplied error detail.
service.sync-error.scope: Composition and UI-sketch session error presentation.
service.sync-error.referent: A service synchronization failure and its message.
service.sync-error.precedence: Generic fallback; revision conflict and wrong session type retain specific recovery messages.
examples: Display a failed request detail during loading or saving.
nonExamples: A revision-conflict message with recovery instructions.

actions.create.meaning: Commit creation of a new item identified by the surrounding dialog.
actions.create.scope: Shared creation confirmation buttons; currently the workspace project form.
actions.create.referent: The new item described by the enclosing form.
actions.create.precedence: Commits creation; does not merely open a creation form or duplicate an existing item.
examples: Create a project after entering its name.
nonExamples: Open the New project dialog.

actions.rename.meaning: Change the display name of an existing item without replacing its identity or contents.
actions.rename.scope: Shared rename menus and dialogs for projects, sessions, and canvas layout states.
actions.rename.referent: The existing project or session selected by the user.
actions.rename.precedence: The menu opens editing; the confirmation commits the edited name. Neither creates a new item nor moves it.
examples: Rename an existing project or session.
nonExamples: Create another project.
Move a session into another project.

actions.move.meaning: Change the container assignment of an existing item while retaining the item and its contents.
actions.move.scope: Container relocation commands; currently workspace session-to-project assignment.
actions.move.referent: The selected item and its destination container; in Workspace, a session and another project.
actions.move.precedence: Not geometric movement on a canvas, copying content, or renaming. Workspace destinations exclude the current project and require an existing project.
examples: Assign an unassigned session to a project.
Move a session to another project.
nonExamples: Drag a canvas node to a new position.
Copy a session.

actions.retry.meaning: Repeat a failed data-loading request for the view identified by the surrounding error state.
actions.retry.scope: Shared recovery buttons in workspace, style-library, and UI-sketch session load failures.
actions.retry.precedence: Retries loading only; does not confirm, recreate, or automatically repeat a potentially destructive mutation. Request ownership does not change the label meaning.
examples: Reload projects after a workspace loading failure.
Reload styles after a style-library loading failure.
Reload the current UI-sketch session after its initial request fails.
nonExamples: Repeat deletion of a style.
Refresh data when no failure occurred.

errors.operation-failed.meaning: A requested mutation failed without a more specific user-facing explanation; the user may try the operation again.
errors.operation-failed.scope: Fallback mutation errors in workspace and style-library dialogs and actions.
errors.operation-failed.referent: The operation initiated by the surrounding control.
errors.operation-failed.precedence: Does not assert that no partial work occurred, promise automatic retries, or replace specific validation and loading errors.
examples: Report failed session renaming.
Report failed style saving.
nonExamples: Report a duplicate project name.
Display a failed initial list load.

session.details.meaning: The shared information panel for the current editing session.
session.details.scope: Shared session-details panel in composition, UI-sketch, and 3D space editors.
session.details.referent: Session metadata and Agent connection controls.
session.details.precedence: Contains metadata fields; not a session name or the canvas tools.
examples: Title the session information panel.
nonExamples: Name a new session.

session.created-at.meaning: The creation timestamp of the persisted session.
session.created-at.scope: Shared session-details panel in composition, UI-sketch, and 3D space editors.
session.created-at.precedence: Distinct from draft edit time and time of the latest save.
examples: Show when the current session was created.
nonExamples: Show the current draft modification time.

session.updated-at.meaning: The modification timestamp loaded from or returned by the service for the current session draft, falling back to the session timestamp when no draft exists.
session.updated-at.scope: Shared session-details panel in composition, UI-sketch, and 3D space editors.
session.updated-at.precedence: Local unsaved edits do not advance this value; the timestamp alone does not certify that all current edits have been saved.
examples: Show the editor modification timestamp.
nonExamples: Report that all changes have been saved.

session.node-count.meaning: The total number of editable draft nodes counted by the current session editor.
session.node-count.scope: Shared session-details panel in composition, UI-sketch, and 3D space editors.
session.node-count.referent: Composition areas, images, focus points and optional direction line; UI-sketch regions, texts and images; or spatial characters and primitive objects.
session.node-count.precedence: Counts model nodes, not DOM elements, project children, or selected items.
examples: Show the current draft node count.
nonExamples: Count selected nodes only.

session.agent-connection-field.meaning: The field identifying controls for connecting an external Agent to the current session.
session.agent-connection-field.scope: Shared session-details panel in composition, UI-sketch, and 3D space editors.
session.agent-connection-field.precedence: Not the creator classification of a style entry or the provenance of a canvas node.
examples: Label the row containing Copy command.
nonExamples: Filter styles created by an Agent.

session.missing-timestamp.meaning: A dash standing in for an unavailable or invalid session timestamp.
session.missing-timestamp.scope: Shared session-details panel in composition, UI-sketch, and 3D space editors.
session.missing-timestamp.referent: A missing or invalid createdAt or updatedAt field.
session.missing-timestamp.precedence: Not a literal stored value, zero nodes, empty user text, or a loading indicator.
examples: Display a dash before session creation time is available.
nonExamples: Display zero when the draft contains no nodes.

canvas.tools.meaning: The controls for adding or manipulating elements in the current editing canvas.
canvas.tools.scope: Composition, UI-sketch, and 3D space tool sections and collapsible canvas side-action panels.
canvas.tools.precedence: Distinct from global navigation actions and session metadata; expand and collapse affect the tool panel, not its elements.
examples: Heading above canvas editing controls.
Accessible name of the canvas tool group.
nonExamples: Workspace New project action area.

shell.sidebar.meaning: The application-level sidebar containing workspace navigation and feature-entry controls.
shell.sidebar.scope: Shared application shell across product pages.
shell.sidebar.referent: The left application sidebar, not a canvas-local tool panel.
shell.sidebar.precedence: Contains navigation; collapsing it changes shell presentation without deleting sessions or hiding draft elements.
examples: Name the application sidebar landmark.
Collapse the workspace sidebar to leave more editing space.
nonExamples: Collapse tools inside the canvas.
Hide a sketch element.

shell.navigation.meaning: The application navigation region presented within the shell sidebar.
shell.navigation.referent: The navigation region containing the supplied workspace sidebar content.
shell.navigation.precedence: Nested within the sidebar; distinct from a single destination label and the surrounding sidebar landmark.
examples: Name the sidebar navigation region for assistive technology.
nonExamples: Name the entire sidebar.
Label the Composition destination.

shell.action-panel.meaning: The page-level panel containing session information and controls for the current editor.
shell.action-panel.scope: The shared shell right-side panel used by composition and UI-sketch pages.
shell.action-panel.precedence: Contains more than canvas tools; expanding or collapsing changes the panel presentation, not session persistence or element visibility. Distinct from the left workspace sidebar.
examples: Show session details and editing controls beside the composition canvas.
nonExamples: Expand the workspace project list.
Hide a region in the final interface stage.

language.interface-selector.meaning: Choose the locale used for the application interface and localized generated copy.
language.interface-selector.scope: The language selector supplied by Human2AiShell to workspace navigation.
language.interface-selector.referent: The active application i18n locale, currently Chinese or English.
language.interface-selector.precedence: Does not translate user-authored notes or select a programming language; locale changes affect application translations.
examples: Switch application translations from Chinese to English.
nonExamples: Rewrite user-entered notes in English.
Select a programming language for generated code.

actions.enter-feature.meaning: Open the feature identified by the surrounding home-page section.
actions.enter-feature.scope: Home-page entry buttons for composition, interface design, and the style library.
actions.enter-feature.referent: The destination feature route shown by the adjacent section heading.
actions.enter-feature.precedence: Navigation only; does not itself request Agent processing, playback, or creation of a persisted session. Distinct from the initial stage of an interface transition.
examples: Open the style library from its home-page section.
Enter the composition workbench.
nonExamples: Select the initial UI-sketch motion stage.
Start an Agent refinement run.

canvas.viewport-zoom.meaning: Change or report the viewing magnification of the canvas without resizing draft elements.
canvas.viewport-zoom.scope: Canvas viewport zoom controls; currently localized through the composition viewport labels.
canvas.viewport-zoom.referent: The viewport zoom factor and its percentage display.
canvas.viewport-zoom.precedence: Presentation only, distinct from changing element area, font size, frame dimensions, or generated output size.
examples: Increase viewing magnification to inspect a small node.
Announce the current zoom percentage.
nonExamples: Increase a region area by 10%.
Increase text font size.

canvas.fit-view.meaning: Adjust the viewport camera and zoom to show the bounds specified by the current editor.
canvas.fit-view.scope: Fit-view controls in composition and UI-sketch canvases.
canvas.fit-view.referent: Composition content bounds or the UI-sketch interface frame bounds.
canvas.fit-view.precedence: Does not resize or move stored draft elements. Composition fits its content bounds; UI sketch fits the interface frame, not every out-of-frame element.
examples: Fit composition content in the viewport.
Fit the UI interface frame while leaving its dimensions unchanged.
nonExamples: Resize the interface frame to match the browser window.
Reset the frame geometry.

canvas.frame-edit-lock.meaning: Prevent or allow direct editing of the current output frame geometry through editor controls.
canvas.frame-edit-lock.scope: Composition frame and UI-sketch interface-frame lock toggles.
canvas.frame-edit-lock.referent: The frame editing lock flag maintained by the current editor.
canvas.frame-edit-lock.precedence: Does not lock viewport pan or zoom, freeze all nodes, or make the persisted session read-only. The button names the next action: unlock while locked and lock while unlocked.
examples: Disable direct movement and resizing of the interface frame while continuing to edit elements.
Unlock the composition frame for geometry changes.
nonExamples: Disable canvas zoom.
Lock a session against concurrent service writes.

session.editor-loading.meaning: Progress feedback while preparing the selected editor and loading its session data.
session.editor-loading.scope: Composition and UI-sketch session editors; default names are also used by workspace creation controls.
session.editor-loading.referent: The composition or interface session being opened.
session.editor-loading.precedence: Transient loading feedback, not an Agent refinement status or a mutation failure.
searchTerms: 正在加载 UI 界面
examples: Announce that a composition session is loading.
nonExamples: Announce that an Agent is processing the draft.

session.new-editor-title.meaning: A fallback page title when the editor does not yet have a session title.
session.new-editor-title.scope: Composition and UI-sketch session editors; default names are also used by workspace creation controls.
session.new-editor-title.referent: The new-session editing context before a session title is available.
session.new-editor-title.precedence: Presentation only; not the default name sent to session creation and not a command to create another session.
examples: Title the editor while sessionTitle is null.
nonExamples: Persist an Untitled composition name during session creation.

session.default-name.meaning: The localized default name supplied when creating a session without a user-entered name.
session.default-name.scope: Composition and UI-sketch session editors; default names are also used by workspace creation controls.
session.default-name.referent: The persisted title of a newly created composition or interface session.
session.default-name.precedence: Unlike a fallback page title, this is sent to the service and can later be renamed; changing interface locale does not itself translate an existing stored title.
examples: Create a composition with its localized default title from the sidebar.
nonExamples: Replace an existing user-authored session title on locale change.

session.draft-revision-conflict.meaning: The submitted draft revision is stale because another operation has already updated the persisted draft; the message reports the latest revision and asks the user to reopen the session.
session.draft-revision-conflict.scope: Composition and UI-sketch session editors; default names are also used by workspace creation controls.
session.draft-revision-conflict.referent: DRAFT_REVISION_CONFLICT and its actualLatestRevision value for the current editor.
session.draft-revision-conflict.precedence: Specific recovery feedback rather than generic synchronization failure; it does not automatically overwrite, merge, or discard local edits.
examples: Report that another operation advanced a draft to revision 7.
nonExamples: Report a network outage without a known revision conflict.

session.editor-type-mismatch.meaning: The requested session has a type incompatible with the editor used to open it.
session.editor-type-mismatch.scope: Composition and UI-sketch session editors; default names are also used by workspace creation controls.
session.editor-type-mismatch.referent: The loaded session type versus the composition or interface editor.
session.editor-type-mismatch.precedence: Different from a missing session, unsupported service endpoint, or corrupted draft; this message does not convert the session to another type.
searchTerms: 不是 UI 界面会话
examples: Reject opening an interface session in the composition editor.
nonExamples: Report that a session identifier does not exist.

app.product-name.meaning: The localized product identity shown by the application.
app.product-name.scope: Browser document title, home-page heading, shared shell product name, and connector or Skill marketplace product identity. The application sidebar brand also links to the home page.
app.product-name.referent: The Human2AI product, named 以形塑形 in Chinese and human2ai in English.
app.product-name.precedence: The product name is distinct from individual feature names, session titles and implementation readiness messages.
examples: Show the product name in the shell and browser title.
nonExamples: Use a session title as the product identity.

canvas.viewport-help.meaning: On-demand instructions for placing nodes, cancelling placement, zooming and panning the editor canvas.
canvas.viewport-help.scope: Composition and UI-sketch viewport help controls.
canvas.viewport-help.referent: The shared one-shot tool placement gestures and InfiniteCanvasViewport wheel, secondary-button drag and Space plus primary-button drag gestures.
canvas.viewport-help.precedence: Selecting a node tool arms placement without creating data; clicking places a default-sized node, dragging sizes a shape or image, and Escape cancels. Panning retains priority over placement. This help does not explain node metadata or frame resizing.
examples: Explain Space plus primary-button drag to pan either editor canvas.
Explain selecting a tool followed by a canvas click or drag, with Escape to cancel.
nonExamples: Explain how arrow keys move a selected node.

canvas.node-description.meaning: A read-only explanation supplied by an Agent of what a canvas node represents and contributes. In composition work it explains the visual relationship and perceptual effect, without becoming the user's revision instruction.
canvas.node-description.scope: Read-only node metadata in composition and UI canvas editors.
canvas.node-description.referent: The user-perceived region, static text, or image represented by the selected node.
canvas.node-description.precedence: It explains the current node's role and remains separate from the editable node note, which carries the user's direction for changing that node. Composition explanations prioritize contribution to the whole over pictured-object identity.
examples: Describe an imported rectangle as the dynamic project-list region while leaving its user note editable.
Explain how a low repeated foreground rhythm supplies scale and overlap, making the main mass feel larger and more distant, while leaving its user note empty.
Explain how a broad lower image mass counterbalances dense type across a gap, rather than merely naming the photographed object.
nonExamples: A user instruction asking the Agent to widen the project list.
The visible static text rendered by a text node.

canvas.node-origin-user.meaning: The immutable canvas node origin for a node created directly by the user in the browser canvas.
canvas.node-origin-user.scope: Read-only node metadata in composition and UI canvas editors.
canvas.node-origin-user.referent: A canvas node whose initial creation action came from the user.
canvas.node-origin-user.precedence: It records original creation only and does not change when an Agent later edits the node.
examples: A rectangle added with the canvas Add region action.
nonExamples: A node proposed by an Agent.
A node imported from an existing UI.

canvas.node-origin-agent.meaning: The immutable canvas node origin for a new design element proposed by an Agent, beyond content already present in the source UI or reference picture.
canvas.node-origin-agent.scope: Read-only node metadata in composition and UI canvas editors.
canvas.node-origin-agent.referent: A new canvas node created by an Agent as design intent.
canvas.node-origin-agent.precedence: It differs from import because the represented element is a new design proposal; editing an imported node does not change its origin to agent.
examples: An Agent adds a proposed status-summary region to a layout draft.
nonExamples: A browser-created user node.
A node imported from an existing UI.

canvas.node-origin-import.meaning: The immutable canvas node origin for an abstract visual element that an Agent recovered from existing project UI or a supplied reference picture.
canvas.node-origin-import.scope: Read-only node metadata in composition and UI canvas editors.
canvas.node-origin-import.referent: A canvas node representing a perceptible region, text, focal point, or visual flow already present in the source UI or picture.
canvas.node-origin-import.precedence: It records recovered content rather than a new proposal. UI projection interprets accepted edits against the existing UI; composition projection records revised visual intent without editing the source picture.
examples: An Agent represents an existing dynamic project list as one imported rectangle.
An Agent represents the main subject or title in a reference picture as an editable composition region.
nonExamples: A screenshot of the old UI.
A newly proposed Agent layout node.

canvas.layer-bring-to-front.meaning: Move selected canvas nodes above all other content nodes.
canvas.layer-bring-to-front.scope: Composition and UI canvas context menus; UI order is shared across motion states.
canvas.layer-bring-to-front.referent: The selected content nodes in the persisted back-to-front stacking order.
canvas.layer-bring-to-front.precedence: Changes visual occlusion only, independently of shot scale, visual weight, numbering, and geometry. Frames, guides and selection controls are excluded.
examples: Bring to front for an image overlapping a region.
nonExamples: Move a node spatially.
Change foreground/background scene depth.

canvas.layer-bring-forward.meaning: Move selected canvas nodes forward by one unselected neighbor, preserving their relative order.
canvas.layer-bring-forward.scope: Composition and UI canvas context menus; UI order is shared across motion states.
canvas.layer-bring-forward.referent: The selected content nodes in the persisted back-to-front stacking order.
canvas.layer-bring-forward.precedence: Changes visual occlusion only, independently of shot scale, visual weight, numbering, and geometry. Frames, guides and selection controls are excluded.
examples: Bring forward for an image overlapping a region.
nonExamples: Move a node spatially.
Change foreground/background scene depth.

canvas.layer-send-backward.meaning: Move selected canvas nodes backward by one unselected neighbor, preserving their relative order.
canvas.layer-send-backward.scope: Composition and UI canvas context menus; UI order is shared across motion states.
canvas.layer-send-backward.referent: The selected content nodes in the persisted back-to-front stacking order.
canvas.layer-send-backward.precedence: Changes visual occlusion only, independently of shot scale, visual weight, numbering, and geometry. Frames, guides and selection controls are excluded.
examples: Send backward for an image overlapping a region.
nonExamples: Move a node spatially.
Change foreground/background scene depth.

canvas.layer-send-to-back.meaning: Move selected canvas nodes below all other content nodes.
canvas.layer-send-to-back.scope: Composition and UI canvas context menus; UI order is shared across motion states.
canvas.layer-send-to-back.referent: The selected content nodes in the persisted back-to-front stacking order.
canvas.layer-send-to-back.precedence: Changes visual occlusion only, independently of shot scale, visual weight, numbering, and geometry. Frames, guides and selection controls are excluded.
examples: Send to back for an image overlapping a region.
nonExamples: Move a node spatially.
Change foreground/background scene depth.

canvas-history.undo.meaning: Restore the preceding complete local canvas operation, including unsaved edits.
canvas-history.undo.scope: Composition, UI sketch and 3D space editor history controls and keyboard actions.
canvas-history.undo.referent: Restore the preceding complete local canvas operation, including unsaved edits.
canvas-history.undo.precedence: Applies to draft content in the current open session; excludes viewport navigation, native text-input undo and historical version browsing. A complete gesture is one operation.
examples: Undo a drag as one operation; redo restores its final position.
nonExamples: Undo each pointer event or move the viewport camera.

canvas-history.redo.meaning: Reapply the next locally undone canvas operation until a new edit replaces that branch.
canvas-history.redo.scope: Composition, UI sketch and 3D space editor history controls and keyboard actions.
canvas-history.redo.referent: Reapply the next locally undone canvas operation until a new edit replaces that branch.
canvas-history.redo.precedence: Applies to draft content in the current open session; excludes viewport navigation, native text-input undo and historical version browsing. A complete gesture is one operation.
examples: Undo a drag as one operation; redo restores its final position.
nonExamples: Undo each pointer event or move the viewport camera.

canvas-history.label.meaning: The pair of controls for local canvas operation history.
canvas-history.label.scope: Composition, UI sketch and 3D space editor history controls and keyboard actions.
canvas-history.label.referent: The pair of controls for local canvas operation history.
canvas-history.label.precedence: Applies to draft content in the current open session; excludes viewport navigation, native text-input undo and historical version browsing. A complete gesture is one operation.
examples: Undo a drag as one operation; redo restores its final position.
nonExamples: Undo each pointer event or move the viewport camera.

canvas.layout-states.meaning: Named, ordered editable layout states of one canvas, sharing node content.
canvas.layout-states.scope: Composition and UI-sketch state controls, state copy menus and UI transition headings.
canvas.layout-states.referent: Persisted state identities, names, order and layout snapshots.
canvas.layout-states.precedence: State selection restores layout without changing shared node content. Composition includes independent frame geometry and layer order; UI retains its existing shared frame and layers. State names and stable numbers persist; UI transitions follow displayed state order.
examples: Rename State 2 to Enabled.
Reorder states without changing their contents.
nonExamples: Start an Agent job.
Play a rendered animation.

canvas.create-state.meaning: Add an editable layout state by copying its source immediately after it.
canvas.create-state.scope: Composition and UI-sketch Add state buttons and New state menus.
canvas.create-state.referent: The ordered layout states of the current canvas.
canvas.create-state.precedence: Copies layout, retains shared node content, selects the new state and persists it through existing draft saving. UI additionally copies per-state visibility.
examples: Add State 2 so its layout can be edited separately.
Use the compact Add state button beside the only state tab; after a second state exists, create further states from the state menu.
nonExamples: Copy the motion implementation prompt.
Start animation playback.

canvas.delete-state.meaning: Remove one editable layout state while preserving shared nodes and all remaining layouts.
canvas.delete-state.scope: Composition and UI-sketch state menus and deletion confirmations.
canvas.delete-state.referent: The targeted state tab and its snapshot.
canvas.delete-state.precedence: Requires confirmation and retains at least one state. Deleting the current state selects a neighboring state; it does not delete the session or shared elements.
examples: Delete an unused expanded state.
nonExamples: Delete all interface nodes.
